business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real-Time Video Matching and Cross-Border Social Telephony

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (University: Kingdom of Spain; état: Estado español)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental); constitutional unitary State with regional private law foral pockets (Catalonia, Navarra, Aragon, Basque Country) and EU law primacy

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC'), arts. 4, 20-22, 58-62, 183-184 and 368; Código de Comercio arts. 116 and 119; Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a los emprendedores (DUE/CIRCE single electronic window); Ley 5/2015 de fomento de la financiación empresarial (notarial and registration procedure).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Notary (Notario) for deed execution; Registro Mercantil Provincial for formal inscription; Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate; all coordinated via the Single Electronic Document (DUE/CIRCE) portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation), filed electronically through the DUE/CIRCE single window and submitted by the notary for inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Sociedad de Limitada requires a minimum capital of EUR 3,000 (LSC art. 4), fully subscribed and fully paid-up at incorporation (LSC arts. 58-59). There is no escrow-account modality; capital is deposited in a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by a banker's certificate (certificado de desembolso). Funds become available upon registration, but distributions may not reduce net assets below the statutory EUR 3,000 floor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the organizational meeting of the incorporators of [●], Sociedad de Limitada, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted: (1) subscription of the entire share capital of EUR 3,000, comprising 3,000 participations of EUR 1.00 nominal value each, fully paid-up in cash; (2) adoption of the registered office at [●], within the territorial jurisdiction of the Registro Mercantil de [●]; (3) appointment of [●] as Sole Administrator and [●] as Secretary, each accepting office; (4) delegation to the Sole Administrator to execute the public deed before the Notary, pay the capital-transfer tax, obtain the provisional and definitive NIF, and complete inscription with the Mercantile Registry and the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain a Negative Name Certificate (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name-certification service accessible through notaries and the DUE/CIRCE electronic window).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically a request stating up to three proposed company names, the S.L. entity type and the registered-office province. The Central Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered. The certificate is valid for three months and must be annexed to the deed.
required_dossiers: Name-certificate application form (solicitud de certificación de denominación social)
Identification of each incorporator (passport or NIE)
Proposed company names and registered-office province
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, the Central Registry issues a negative certification; the applicant resubmits with the remaining alternative names or fresh options and pays the corresponding certificate fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Provisional Bank Account and Deposit the Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized Spanish credit institution supervised by the Banco de España.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account in the name of the company 'en formación' (company in formation) using the provisional NIF or the future corporate name, deposit not less than EUR 3,000, and request a banker's certificate (certificado de desembolso) stating the depositor, amount and account number. The certificate is annexed to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF certificate issued by AEAT (if already obtained)
Passports or NIEs of the incorporators
Bank account-opening mandate and draft statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank refuses to open the provisional account, another credit institution may be chosen; alternatively, a notarial deposit suffices, provided that the statutory minimum capital is certified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) of the notarial district of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name certificate, banker's capital-deposit certificate, draft Articles of Association and identification of all incorporators. The notary verifies legal capacity, approves the by-laws (Estatutos) covering data processing, hosting and video-match platform services (CNAE 6311), executes the deed and protocolizes it.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (certificado de denominación social)
Banker's certificate of paid-up capital
Draft Articles of Association in Spanish
Passports or NIEs of all incorporators
Evidence of corporate capacity and authorizations, if any incorporator is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to a clause, the draft by-laws are amended and re-executed; formal defects are cured by corrective resolution before proceeding to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay the Capital Transfer and Documented Legal Acts Tax (IAJD/ITPAJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad Autónoma (regional tax office of the registered-office region).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days following execution, self-assess the 'Modalidad Actos Jurídicos Documentados' (0.5%-1.0% of the nominal subscribed capital, depending on the autonomous community) using Model 600 and the first copy of the deed, presented at the regional tax office or via its electronic office.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Form 600 (declaración-liquidación) for IAJD
DIC (declaración informativa) or incorporator identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment triggers surcharges and interest; the taxpayer files the corrected Model 600 with the regional office and may apply for installment or challenge the assessment if the tax authorities calculate the tax base differently.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Mercantile Registry (Inscripción Registral)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located, coordinated with the Registro Mercantil Central through the CIRCE/DUE system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first copy of the notarial deed together with proof of IAJD payment to the Mercantile Registry within one month of execution. The registrar reviews the incorporation, and upon approval issues the registration certificate; the company acquires full legal personality on this date.
required_dossiers: First copy of the deed of incorporation
Proof of IAJD payment (Model 600 receipt)
Annexed negative name certificate
Power of attorney or identification of the appointed administrator, as requested by the registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registrar issues a calificación listing defects; the notary executes a corrective deed (escritura de subsanación) and resubmits. If the decision is final and negative, an appeal lies to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within the statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Definite NIF and Complete Tax Census Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), local or electronic office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile registration, file Model 036 to obtain the definitive NIF (replacing the provisional one), enroll the company in the Census of Entrepreneurs, select the IAE epígrafe corresponding to ISIC 6311, and complete the VAT census declarations if intra-Community operations are foreseen.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Mercantile Registry inscription
Copy of the notarial deed
Provisional NIF certificate
Identification of the appointed administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT withholds the definitive NIF pending verification of the registered office, provide a lease agreement or utility bill; if the census data is deficient, correct the Model 036 and resubmit to the competent local AEAT office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Employer Registration and Occupational Risk Prevention (PRL) Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and the appointed administrator/company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer (inscripción de la empresa), obtain the employer account code (CCC), declare the opening of the workplace to the provincial labour authority, and implement the PRL plan under Ley 31/1995, including workplace risk assessment and fire-safety arrangements, before starting operations.
required_dossiers: Definitive NIF certificate
Mercantile Registry certificate of incorporation
Lease contract or title to the premises
PRL plan and workplace risk assessment
Social-security numbers of directors and prospective employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incomplete submissions suspend the CCC allocation; the company corrects the filing through the Sistema RED and secures a certified PRL workplace assessment; reinspection of fire-safety measures must be requested from the municipal fire brigade.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6311 (data processing, hosting and video-matching platform) has no industrial-plant regulator. If the company leases administrative offices, the competent authority is the local Ayuntamiento (municipality) for a 'declaración responsable de inicio de actividad' under the transposition of Directive 2006/123/EC (Ley 12/2012).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is required for the video-chat social-telephony scope; the only physical-paper instrument is the municipal 'declaración responsable' (or a 'licencia de apertura' if the autonomous community so prescribes) for office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD), with the respective Comunidad Autónoma acting as competent project authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no Environmental Impact Assessment required: Ley 21/2013 Annexes II and III do not list digital data-processing or platform activities, and the company generates no physical environmental project footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial process discharges or VOC emissions. Applicable thresholds are limited to municipal acoustic comfort (approximately 35 dBA at the facade), commercial waste segregation and management under Ley 7/2022 through authorized waste managers, and WEEE/RoHS obligations (RD 110/2015) for end-of-life office IT equipment only.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: premises must comply with the Código Técnico de la Edificación (DB-SI); buildings over 6 metres in height or housing more than 200 occupants require the Inspección Técnica de Edificios and municipal bomberos conformity. Occupational: full compliance with Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including a written risk assessment, workstation ergonomics under RD 486/1997, fire-evacuation plans, and appointment of a PRL service; the workplace-opening declaration is filed with the provincial labour authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Tributaria, the Spanish Tax Agency with official portal at https://www.agenciatributaria.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign or domestic entities must procure a NIF by registering with the Agencia Tributaria through the online portal or in person, providing corporate documentation, proof of legal address, and identification documents; non-residents may use NIE initially and convert to NIF upon establishment of economic activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate check-the-box elections; however, hybrid mismatch election rules apply under Council Directive (EU) 2017/828, and certain income may qualify for territorial tax regime treatment under specific statutory provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 50,000 EUR in annual taxable supplies triggering mandatory registration with the Agencia Tributaria
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory implementation of electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) with real-time transmission to the AEAT, digital stamps, and clearance procedures; large taxpayers must integrate via API with the SII (Immediate Supply Information) system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for 0% VAT rate on exports of goods outside the EU or intra-EU supplies under reverse charge mechanism; for cross-border services, zero-rating applies to supplies made to non-EU customers without establishment in Spain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment from foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims result in penalties of up to 100% of the erroneously zero-rated VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of benefits with potential administrative sanctions and criminal prosecution for intentional misrepresentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain). Under the Single Supervisory Mechanism of the ECB for credit institutions; authorizes credit institutions, e-money institutions, and payment institutions; the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Infringements (SEPBLAC) enforces AML/CTF supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible in Spain. Capital and current account movements are liberalized pursuant to EU Treaty Articles 63-66 TFEU, Directive 88/361/EEC, and Spanish Law 19/2003 (Régimen Jurídico de los Movimientos de Capitales). No prior administrative authorization, foreign-exchange permit, or conversion license is required for inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, outbound trade payments, profit remittance, or dividend distributions. Freely usable EUR and foreign-currency accounts may be opened at authorized Spanish credit institutions. Dividend and profit remittance obstacles are limited to tax: 25% Spanish Corporate Income Tax on the SL plus Non-Resident Income Tax withholding on distributions (subject to double-tax treaty relief). Spain maintains statistical reporting obligations under Order EHA/3378/2011: any cross-border payment or collection equal to or exceeding EUR 1,250,000 must be declared to Banco de España within 15 calendar days of the transaction date; monthly EA (foreign-currency) position balances exceeding EUR 50 million must be declared under model A-10 by the last day of the following month. These declarations are statistical only and do not constitute exchange-control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain imposes no export-proceeds surrender ratio, mandatory conversion timeline, or repatriation quota. The SL (including the video-match app) may freely retain, convert, or disburse EUR and foreign-currency receipts in any settlement currency. The only cross-border obligation is the statistical declaration (1) for each transaction equal to or above EUR 1,250,000 (submission within 15 calendar days), and (2) for foreign-currency balances above EUR 50 million at month-end. Export receipts routed through Apple IAP (Apple Distribution International) and Paymentwall are treated as cross-border service export collections and are subject to the same statistical thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency Account (Cuenta Operativa) plus segregated Capital Escrow/Settlement Sub-Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. (BBVA, Madrid)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in EUR/USD with onboarding via BBVA Open Platform; Capital Escrow Account for shareholder injection
Operational IBAN Account and merchant settlement account for Paymentwall/Apple IAP collections
Operational Account with SEPA Instant access; Capital Escrow Account available
Operational Account only; limited cross-border fintech appetite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for secondary treasury rails; Medium for core settlement. EEA-authorized electronic money institutions and payment institutions may passport into Spain under the EBA register and open Spanish IBANs at Banco de España-licensed entities. Digital EMIs (e.g., Verto, Multitude, Connectum, and Spanish-licensed EMI such as Pismo) provide faster onboarding, multi-currency virtual IBANs, and API-driven clearing; however, an EMI is legally prohibited from extending credit and must safeguard client funds in a credit institution. For the Medium_Risk_Enhanced video-match app profile, core salary and tax payments should flow through a tier-1 commercial bank; the EMI/PSP rails are viable for receivables concentration, FX conversion at scale, and payout to overseas content moderators. Paymentwall as a payment facilitator and Apple's App Store settlement operate outside the banking license perimeter but their settlement flows must land in a Banco de España-regulated account. Legal restriction: any operation involving an unregulated offshore digital EMI without EEA passport is considered non-viable and creates UBO/KYC blockers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for every director, but practical onboarding requires a Spanish notarized power-of-attorney for the authorized signatories. Spanish Law 10/2010 (art. 3-4) mandates identification and due diligence; Law 18/2022 permits remote video identification (VCI) using qualified electronic signatures, and tier-1 banks now accept remote corporate account opening with a video interview. In market practice, Banco Santander and BBVA require a one-off virtual compliance interview with the CEO/CFO and the notarized POA (executed before any notary worldwide, then apostilled). Non-EU resident directors or individuals holding UBO status must undergo enhanced due diligence, including passport verification by video call and source-of-funds evidence. Physical presence at a Spanish branch is highly likely to be requested within 3-6 months for the signing of additional mandates or for receipt of a corporate card; if directors reside in Latin America, the bank may accept a branch-notarized POA at BBVA/Santander's local subsidiary. The safe protocol is: notarized POA + apostille + certified Spanish translation, then a virtual interview scheduled with the bank's corporate/IBD compliance desk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model flagged as Medium_Risk_Enhanced: anonymous, real-time random video matching with high-frequency in-app microtransactions processed through Apple IAP and Paymentwall, non-face-to-face user KYC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Paymentwall Merchant Services Agreement; detailed transaction-flow diagram; app architecture and moderation/age-verification policy; anti-fraud and real-time content-monitoring protocols; enterprise compliance contact sheet; documented statement that all merchants-of-record (Apple/Paymentwall) perform end-user KYC in their acquiring layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is non-EU resident (e.g., Latin America or US) with foreign ownership chain above 25%, including a foreign holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration under Law 10/2010 art. 4; certified corporate registry extracts and chain-of-title documents; valid passport copies; 6-month source-of-funds bank statements from a recognized foreign institution; certificate of tax residence for each UBO; apostille/legalization; professional Spanish translation; board resolution approving the UBO list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue volatility: unpredictable weekly spikes in App Store/IAP settlements and Paymentwall payouts disproportionate to stated workforce and physical footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month business plan with traffic/user-acquisition forecasts; Apple App Store Connect financial reports; Paymentwall settlement statements; server/datacenter invoices (AWS/GCP); explanation of revenue recognition cycles; payroll and contractor registers; monthly cash-flow projections; treasury policy for merchant-settlement reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of a statutory license: classifying the video-match app as unregulated, potentially triggering obligations under the Spanish General Telecommunications Law (Ley 9/2014) or the CNMC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal memorandum from Spanish counsel confirming the service qualifies as an information-society service (Ley 34/2002, LSSI-CE) requiring only the mandatory notice to CNMC (declaración responsable), not a telecom license; GDPR compliance dossier with DPO designation; AEPD registration references (if personal data processed); ISO/IEC 27001 certificate; CNMC communication acknowledgment receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The account is expected to receive intermingled capital injections, shareholder loans, and operating revenue, while making outbound disbursements to overseas content moderators and related parties in Latin America.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated account usage matrix; board-approved treasury policy; intercompany loan agreements with interest-rate terms (OECD-compliant transfer pricing); counterparty whitelist; sanction-screening protocol with a list of sanctioned-country restrictions; record-keeping policy satisfying Law 10/2010's 10-year archival requirement; periodic AML officer reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance concern: the SL has a registered office in Spain but directors and owner-operators are digital nomads or non-residents, raising shell-company indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid office lease or coworking membership invoice; Spanish payroll and Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social) registration records; employment contracts of Spanish-resident staff; management-meeting minutes in Spain; Spanish supplier contracts; corporate tax filings (Modelo 200/303); evidence of actual economic activity such as Spanish bank account usage with local operating expenses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended rail: SWIFT MT103 with full structured remittance information. For equity injection from a foreign shareholder, use Banco de España statistical concept code A1 (Direct Investment — Equity); for shareholder loan funding, use code B1 (Financial Credit between Group Companies). The sending bank must include the beneficiary ES IBAN, the exact legal name 'ES_SL' (or equivalent registered corporate name), bank identifier of the Spanish tier-1 institution, and the /OCMT/ or /INV/ purpose-code field. All inflows above EUR 1,250,000 trigger the 15-calendar-day statistical declaration to Banco de España (model A), which the relationship bank will coordinate. For Apple IAP revenue, the clearing rail is not a wire: Apple Distribution International settles funds to the SL's IBAN via SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) or wire in the revenue currency; treasury must reconcile these merchant settlements separately. For Paymentwall payouts (typically USD), the inbound rail is an SWIFT MT103 from Paymentwall's US/EU partner bank to the SL's USD counterpart at the Spanish bank; include the merchant settlement reference and 'INV' purpose code. Verification steps: (1) confirm the originator is an authorized intermediary/financial institution with no OFAC/EU-sanctioned nexus; (2) match the settlement reference with the Paymentwall/Apple dashboard; (3) if the amount exceeds EUR 1.25M or USD equivalent, pre-notify the Banco de España statistical desk and ensure the bank files model A; (4) document the economic substance of each inbound wire with a board-approved source-of-funds memo.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Intra-EU vendor and salary disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer with the beneficiary IBAN; no SWIFT message required for SEPA-zone payments. Non-EU supplier payments, cloud/telecom services, content-moderation fees, insurance, and legal fees in Latin America or North America: SWIFT MT103 with UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference), using the correspondent network of the tier-1 Spanish bank. For high-value treasury centralization, SWIFT MT202 COV is acceptable for interbank transfers between the SL's own accounts. Commercial letters of credit are not needed for the services business model; the appropriate instrument is an irrevocable documentary credit only if the SL later resells physical hardware or enters into a distribution/warehousing trade flow through Spain into Latin America. All outbound cross-border disbursements must include accurate purpose-of-payment codes aligned with the Banco de España statistical classification (e.g., code B3 for imported services, code A4 for operational transfers). Payments to prohibited or high-risk jurisdictions must be blocked at the onboarding stage; the treasury policy must maintain a maintainable audit trail at law 10/2010's 10-year retention standard. For Apple IAP settlement reversals and Paymentwall chargebacks, use their respective PSP settlement reversals rather than outbound SWIFT messages.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX Forward (vanilla) with a Banco de España-regulated tier-1 credit institution under a 1992/2002 ISDA Master Agreement and CSA, with maturity matched to the forecasted USD payout cycle from Paymentwall; maximum tenor 24 months; margin/collateral in EUR cash.
EUR/USD FX Swap (FXS) for rolling conversion of temporary USD inflows into EUR operating liquidity, executed under the same ISDA/CSA; no unauthorized speculative position.

Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) EUR/USD for balance-sheet hedging of committed USD revenue streams (12-24 months), economically converting future Paymentwall USD settlements into fixed-rate EUR cash flows; permitted for treasury hedging only.

OTC plain-vanilla EUR/USD options (purchased, non-writing) for tail-risk protection on large latent settlements from App Store/Paymentwall; execution through an EU MiFID II-authorised investment firm.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — permissible only for genuinely inconvertible or low-liquidity Latin American currencies (e.g., USD/COP, USD/ARS) arising from user payment collection in those jurisdictions; EUR/USD and other fully convertible-currency NDFs are legally permissible but operationally unnecessary, and the policy is to reject them in favor of deliverable forwards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the province of the registered office (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the ordinary general meeting; such approval must occur within six months after the fiscal year end. For a calendar-year-end entity, the filing deadline is 31 July annually.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a registered warning and fines of EUR 60 to EUR 600 per day; the company suffers 'cierre registral' preventing registration of corporate acts; failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years leads to closure of the registry file and may precipitate administrative strike-off after dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria – AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days of the expiration of the six-month period following the end of the tax year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the due date is 25 July annually.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs progressive surcharges under Article 27 LGT (5% up to 3 months, 10% up to 6 months, 15% up to 12 months, 20% thereafter plus late-payment interest); penalties under Article 191 LGT may reach 50%–100% of the amount evaded; asset seizure and bankruptcy proceedings may follow sustained non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Declaration and Ownership Record Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry – Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted simultaneously with the deposit of annual accounts; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false UBO statements are subject to administrative fines under Law 10/2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering, ranging from EUR 300 to EUR 500,000 or more, and may cause suspension of registry approvals for corporate decisions and share transfers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit of annual accounts is required for an SL that exceeds at least two of the following three criteria on the closing date of two consecutive fiscal years: (i) total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; (iii) average number of employees exceeding 50. Audit is also mandatory for companies in regulated sectors or with a listed group parent even if thresholds are not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) effective under Royal Decree 1514/2007; consolidated accounts use EU-adopted IFRS; non-listed individual entities apply PGC Local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For every Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the entity must maintain an internal updated register of ultimate beneficial owners. At the time of depositing annual accounts, the company must confirm the continuing accuracy of its UBO registry (including share transfer changes) with the Mercantile Registry. Any share transfer or indirect ownership change requires an update to the UBO register and a formal filing with the Registro de Titularidades Reales within 30 days. The annual confirmation is mandatory regardless of whether ownership has changed during the fiscal year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members – Libro Registro de Socios
Register of Directors – Libro Registro de Administradores
Accounting Daily and Inventory Books – Libros de Contabilidad (Diario e Inventario y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typical annual registered office and corporate agent fee range in Spain: USD 110–340 (EUR 100–300), depending on provider and level of compliance support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical certified audit fee for a small SL near the audit threshold or voluntarily audited: USD 3,000–8,000; fees vary with turnover, group complexity, and foreign transactions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly created entities subject to qualifying conditions (first two taxable periods with positive tax base and commencement of activity); 10% reduced rate for entities under the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) regime qualifying under the Estatuto de la Empresa Familiar or micro-enterprise rules where applicable; R&D and technological innovation tax credits up to 25-42% of qualifying expenditure; deductions for job creation for disabled employees; reduction for intangible assets under patent box regime (effective rate can drop to approximately 9.375% for qualifying IP income); no general statutory tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) online platform (Sede Electrónica), using mandatory electronic filing for all entities subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-fiscal-year-end period. For fiscal years ending 31 December, the deadline is 1 July through 25 July of the subsequent year. Non-calendar fiscal year ends follow the six-month plus 25-day rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF), corporate name, fiscal address, and dominant entity status for tax consolidation groups.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Spanish permanent establishment (PE) NIF or the non-resident entity's NIF-Representante (NIF-REP) if filing through a representative; no alternative identification accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after application of prior-year loss carryforwards and tax consolidation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident entities with a PE, compute the taxable base attributable to the PE under the arm's length principle and the activity carried on in Spain; deductions for head-office expenses limited to 50% of the PE's taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability calculated by applying the statutory rate (default 25%) to the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same rate for PE income; verify if the applicable DTA (e.g., Spain-Luxembourg, Spain-Netherlands, Spanish domestic law for non-residents) provides a lower rate or exemption for business profits only if the PE's existence meets the DTA permanent establishment threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International double taxation relief for taxes paid abroad on income sourced outside Spain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the ordinary deduction method (tax paid abroad) or the exemption method for qualifying foreign income; attach Form 296 or supporting commitments and compute the deduction based on the lower of foreign tax paid or Spanish tax applicable to the foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting tax liability after credits, withholdings, and installment payments (pagos fraccionados).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident entity's PE is liable, the quarterly installment payments (Modelo 202) must be reconciled; final payment must accompany the Modelo 200 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Installment payments already made during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs are subject to the same installment payment rules; if the parent entity elects for the instalment option based on prior-year liability, indicate the applicable option in the corresponding annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits for R&D, technological innovation, audiovisual production, and digital content creation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available for activities effectively carried out through a Spanish PE; expenses incurred abroad by the head office are not eligible unless attributable to the PE under the permanent establishment's functional economic substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount due if filed within three months of the deadline, with an additional 5% for each full three-month period or fraction (up to 20% maximum). Surcharge of 1% per month of delay (plus annual late payment interest of 3.75% in 2024) for settlements after the deadline. Failure to file within 12 months incurs a 2% late-payment surcharge plus interest and potential closure of the tax file; formal infraction penalties from €1,500 to €15,000 for failure to provide required documentation, plus daily surcharges for non-compliance with electronic filing obligations (up to €1,000 per day if administrative requirement persists).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner (non-resident shareholder) must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the tax authority of the residence country, usually valid for the calendar year of the dividend payment. The certificate must be submitted to the Spanish paying entity before the dividend distribution or, at the latest, before the filing of the withholding tax return (Modelo 216) for the quarter in which the dividend is paid. A single certificate may cover multiple payments within one calendar year if generated by the foreign competent authority (e.g., Form 6166 for US, Form 8802 for the US, or standard Form 10 for EU tax residents). The paying entity applies the reduced DTA rate at source upon receipt; if excess withholding is applied, the non-resident must file a refund claim under the DTA or the Spanish non-resident tax regulations within the applicable limitation period (generally four years). For dividends paid to EU parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) exemption may apply with zero WHT, subject to a minimum 5% shareholding held for at least one year, and the parent entity's active substance and anti-abuse compliance (Spanish anti-hybrid rules).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 19% under Spanish domestic law. Under the Interest and Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC), EU-associated companies (25% direct minimum shareholding held for at least one year) may benefit from a 0% WHT on qualifying royalty and interest payments, provided the beneficial owner is subject to corporate tax without exemption and has economic substance. Treaty rates vary: e.g., Spain-Luxembourg DTA caps interest and royalties at 10%; Spain-Netherlands DTA caps royalties at 5% and interest at 10%; Spain-US DTA caps royalties at 8-10% and interest at 5-10% depending on the type and relationship. For royalties deriving from software, patents, trademarks, or know-how, the Spanish tax law requires the beneficial owner to be the formal and economic owner of the IP; if the IP is held through a conduit jurisdiction without substance, the DTA relief may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 aggregate annual transaction value for mandatory Local File and Master File (applicable for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2016 under RDL 634/2015). Entities with revenue below EUR 10 million are exempt from the documentation obligation, but must still apply the arm's length principle and may be required to submit Form 232 (annual TP disclosure) if related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) / Precio Comparable no Ajustado
Resale Price Method / Método del Precio de Reventa
Cost Plus Method / Método del Coste Incrementado
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) / Método del Margen Neto Transaccional
Profit Split Method / Método de Reparto de Beneficios
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Spanish Economic Substance Regulations are embedded in the general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) under Article 15 of the Corporate Income Tax Act (LIS), the anti-hybrid rules, and the substantial requirements for applying EU Directives (parent-subsidiary and interest-royalties). For a Spanish SL engaged in video platform activities, the 'digital presence' concept under the Significant Digital Presence (SDEP) rules introduced by Law 4/2023 requires a deemed permanent establishment when digital services exceed EUR 3 million in taxable revenues, have more than 100,000 users, or enter into more than 3,000 business-to-business digital contracts. The Economic Substance Regulations also require that the Spanish entity maintains adequate personnel, offices, and decision-making functions for the core income-generating activities (IP ownership, user data management, and payment processing). The Spanish tax administration applies the 'substance over form' doctrine to deny treaty or directive benefits to purely letterbox companies with no substantive digital or operational presence, in alignment with the OECD BEPS Action 6 minimum standard.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Understatement of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Apple IAP or Paymentwall settlement revenue from the Modelo 200, falsifying books, or artificially inflating deductible expenses through fake invoices or round-tripping transactions with related service providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax understated, plus late payment interest, and a mandatory penalty surcharge of 20% for the use of means that obscure or impede tax control. Criminal liability under Organic Law 10/1995 (Criminal Code Art. 305) applies when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the corporate tax debt under Article 42 of the General Tax Law (LGT 58/2003) when they were responsible for the unlawful acts and failed to exercise diligent management. Criminal sanctions include imprisonment, disgorgement of profits, and loss of eligibility for public subsidies or contracts; the corporate veil may be pierced under the 'levantamiento del velo' doctrine, and a travel ban may be issued for criminal non-committal. For tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000, the director's personal liberty is at risk; civil liability extends to damages caused to the Treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox SL that merely holds the Spanish tax residence and digital platform licence while the real management and substantive activity is performed by a parent in a zero-tax jurisdiction, especially using the Spanish entity to claim EU resident status without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Spanish GAAR, the tax administration may recharacterize the arrangement and assert a deemed permanent establishment, resulting in taxation of full worldwide income at 25% with surcharges of up to 35%. The Shell Companies Directive if enacted in the future, or current anti-abuse rules under Article 15 LIS, allow the denial of tax benefits and the imposition of a penalty of 30% to 300% of the tax avoided, plus potential inclusion on the public list of defaulters (listado de morosos).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structure the entity to abuse the tax treaty network or the Spanish tax residence are jointly liable for the tax deficiency and penalties; criminal liability may arise under the corporate crime provisions for intentionally violating tax regulations. A court may prohibit the director from practising professional activities related to the entity's trade for up to six years, and the criminal fine may be charged to the director personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-risk payment flows via Paymentwall or Apple IAP without implementing customer due diligence (CDD), transaction monitoring for 6311 industry patterns, or without reporting suspicious transactions to the Spanish Financial Intelligence Unit (SEPBLAC), particularly where the video-chat platform is used for money laundering or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010 on Prevention of Money Laundering, administrative fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 (or 3% of turnover if higher) for severe infractions; suspension of activity for up to 10 years. Criminal liability for money laundering (Art. 301-302 Criminal Code) carries imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and fines of up to triple the laundered amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML failings under the 'compliance officer' liability doctrine; criminal sanctions include imprisonment for money laundering facilitation, personal fines, and forfeiture of illicit gains. SEPBLAC may impose a travel ban on non-resident directors if they leave Spain while under investigation, and the court may bar them from managing financial or financial-technology entities for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, maintain, or file the Local File, Master File, and Form 232 country-by-country information, or entering into related-party transactions (e.g., with the parent's IP holding company in a zero-tax jurisdiction) at non-arm's length prices without economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 15% of the amount of the related-party transaction for failure to provide TP documentation (minimum EUR 10,000 per infraction). For unjustified income adjustment, primary tax correction applies plus a penalty of 50% of the amount assessed; if the documentation is supplied but valuations are incorrect, a penalty of 10% of the value of the transactions applies. Failure to file Form 232 incurs a EUR 300 fine per data field but no less than EUR 1,500 and no more than EUR 15,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the omission or fraudulent documentation may be jointly liable for the TP adjustment and penalties. In cases where the manipulation is linked to tax evasion exceeding EUR 120,000, criminal liability under Art. 305 carries prison sentences; the director's personal bank accounts may be seized under the civil liability order in criminal proceedings, and a prohibition on leaving Spanish territory may be imposed until the tax debt is secured.
